look_here_first: SOUTHERN CRABGRASS (*Digitaria ciliaris*) — START WITH LIGULE: fold blade back to find a true whitish translucent MEMBRANE with JAGGED free edge, roughly 1–3(–4) mm (Williamson County var. ciliaris), not a tuft of external hairs. Next verify sheath/collar hair placement (sheath often hairy, blade comparatively sparse, no auricles); THEN follow 3–7 one-sided tight fingerlike flowering racemes and the paired mature spikelets on a winged axis. Hidden face of UPPER GLUME should be seen and measured to compare with nearly identical D. sanguinalis. Current five local photos cover head and spikelet but NOT the inner true ligule or glume dissection. Roots intentionally after aboveground anatomy. Introduced/non-native status and BONAP county review unchanged.

best_field_traits: Fingerlike raceme cluster supports D. ciliaris, often 2–12 branches (Texas local key often 3–7). Two spikelets occur at each raceme node, with unequal stalks; the small lower glume (~0.2–0.4 mm) and upper glume (about two-thirds to three-quarters spikelet length) are technical details not resolved in our photographs. Annual habit/roots at lower nodes, membranous ligule and smooth lateral sterile lemma nerves add confirmation. An introduced-versus-native conclusion is controlled by the existing project policy, not by these photos.
Annual or short-lived plant with sprawling, decumbent lower stems that can root at nodes, often forming patches.
Terminal seedhead with several roughly fingerlike, often subdigitate one-sided flowering racemes, commonly about 3–7, though counts vary.
Paired stalked spikelets on the underside/one side of a narrow, somewhat winged branch (rachis); paired spikelets and unequal stalks can be resolved with a macro.
Leaf blades frequently about 5–9 mm wide in Central Texas treatments; longer basal blade hairs may occur, so grass hairiness alone is not a species key.
TRUE ligule a whitish, semitranslucent MEMBRANE around 1–3(–4) mm long, often irregularly jagged at top. Confirm at the sheath–blade joint.
Very small lower glume and longer upper glume accompany two-flowered spikelets with a sterile lower and fertile upper floret.
Sterile lower lemma lateral nerves tend to be smooth or only sparsely prickly in this taxon; need 10–20× examination to distinguish some other crabgrass species.
morphology_keys.comparison_training: Large crabgrass (D. sanguinalis) has more prickles on the sterile lemma lateral veins, often with hairier upper leaves. Smooth crabgrass (D. ischaemum) usually has smaller spikelets. Goosegrass (Eleusine indica) has a flattened whitish crown and dense, zipperlike rows of spikelets.
crew_field_check: Start with the new full-head image: see fingerlike clustered racemes and one-sided dense spikelet arrangement.
Compare the new close raceme image with the ORIGINAL original green spikelet macro: these show different scales of the same general anatomy; none proves paired stalks without enough magnification.
On a fresh mature branch at 10–20× COUNT two spikelets at each node and their unequal pedicels; photograph the winged rachis.
Expose a true transparent membranous ligule at blade/sheath joint (1–3 mm) and real rooted lower node on a permitted rooted plant.
If D. sanguinalis is a possibility, dissect a ripe sterile lower lemma and view its lateral veins and ornamentation. If not resolved, use Digitaria sp.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: Whole rooted living plant showing creeping node roots, plus overhead raceme cluster (same individual)
Two attached spikelets per rachis node with unequal stalks and the winged branch in a 1-mm-scale macro
Transparent 1–3 mm membranous ligule exactly at blade/sheath junction, ruler and sheath hairs
Detached lower and upper glumes and sterile lower lemma dorsal veins at 10–20×
True D. sanguinalis vs D. ciliaris comparative sterile lower-lemma vein prickles and hair pattern with vouchered ripe specimen

comparisons.key_distinctions: Against the installed D. cognata, look for tightly imbricate green or brown spikelets arranged on several near-parallel one-sided fingerlike RACEMES rather than fuzzy solitary units at the tips of a giant branching panicle. Against uninstalled D. sanguinalis and D. ischaemum, use the mature sterile lemma lateral nerves/prickles and measured spikelet differences, not whether the plant looks hairy. Goosegrass (Eleusine indica) can also make fingers but has flat zipper-like rows of many distinct florets and whitish compressed basal culms.

diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.look_here_first: Southern crabgrass: follow 3–7 fingerlike one-sided racemes to paired stalked spikelets at each rachis node. Confirm the small lower glume and mature sterile lower-lemma veins under magnification; do not separate crabgrass species from hairiness or head shape alone.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.growth_form: Fibrous-rooted annual or short-lived plant, sprawling or decumbent, sometimes rooting at lower nodes. Blade/sheath junction has a true whitish membranous ligule approximately 1–3(–4) mm and no auricles; collar may be puberulent.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.spikelet_glume_lemma_awn: Williamson County var. ciliaris treatment: 3–7 racemes approximately 25–120 mm long, two spikelets per node on unequal pedicels (~0.4–0.6 and 1.1–4.5 mm). Tiny lower glume ~0.3–0.4 mm, upper glume ~1.7–2 mm and 3-veined. Sterile lower lemma ~2.3–2.7 mm and (5–)7-veined; firm fertile upper lemma ~2.6–3.2 mm, palea ~2 mm. No true lemma or glume awns; do not misidentify ciliate hairs as awns. Regional measurements describe var. ciliaris, not every variety.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.lookalikes: Digitaria sanguinalis can share fingerlike racemes but differs in sterile lower-lemma lateral-nerve ornamentation and hair patterns; D. ischaemum often has smaller spikelets. Installed D. cognata has a more diffuse, many-branched flowering architecture. Eleusine indica bears compact zipperlike multiflowered spikelets and often a whitish flattened base.
precise_photo_arrow_gaps: Rooted same-plant spreading annual with one visibly rooting lower node and full terminal raceme cluster, centimeter ruler.
One attached raceme node with both spikelets and UNEQUAL pedicels and winged rachis at 10–20×, 1-mm scale.
Separate lower glume (0.3–0.4 mm), upper glume, sterile lower lemma and fertile upper lemma/palea on measured macro; label only verified pixels.
Transparent 1–3(–4) mm true ligule and collar at actual blade/sheath junction with ruler.
Vouchered matched D. sanguinalis sterile lower-lemma lateral nerves/prickles, not merely different sheath hairs.
diagnostic_species_finalization_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Preserve one archived original photograph, two credited externally linked panels, eight existing gross-feature arrows, source/license records and existing Old World/range guardrails. field_photo_quickcheck.heading: Southern crabgrass — LIGULE FIRST, then collar/sheath, hidden glume and fingerlike racemes
steps: 1. FIRST ask for a photo not yet on the card: open the INNER blade/sheath junction, expose the continuous transparent jagged-edge 1–3(–4) mm MEMBRANE. Do not mistake exterior sheath hairs or the hair fringe of a different grass for the true ligule.

2. SECOND: photograph the same blade base, OUTER collar, and complete upper sheath from front/back with 1-mm bar; note where hairs truly originate and confirm NO auricles. Do not infer from the grass flower images.

3. Only THEN use currently archived indices 1–2 for fingerlike flowering head, index 4 for true one-sided spikelet rachis, index 3 for the intact spikelet with adjacent uncalibrated scale divisions. No extra distant flowers needed.

4. Photograph mature intact spikelet BACK/HIDDEN upper-glume face and dissect lower/upper glumes, lower sterile lemma and firm fertile lemma. Verify against D. sanguinalis same maturity with 1-mm ruler. One spikelet contains TWO florets, not two spikelets.
5. The three currently archived comparison indices 5–7 are only D. cognata (airy panicle), NOT D. sanguinalis or D. ischaemum; don't transfer their structures or licenses to southern crabgrass.
6. Roots are now lower priority: after ligule and spikelet proof, get one whole flowering plant with a photographed actual node rooting at soil contact, rather than just a prostrate stem.
7. Use individual photo rights for any new source; DO NOT copy UF IFAS/USGS images just because they are visible online. Source attributions and physical source photo bytes required for Learner.

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 01 · LIGULE FIRST — OPEN THE INNER SHEATH
field_id_short_tiles.short: Whitish, translucent membranous ligule, jagged free margin, about 1–3(–4) mm in Central Texas.
field_id_short_tiles.details: GENTLY fold the blade away from the sheath and view INSIDE the blade–sheath junction. Real *D. ciliaris* var. ciliaris has a single broadly convex pale, semitransparent MEMBRANE, with irregularly jagged/erose apex; these are NOT fine ligule hairs. Regional Williamson County treatment gives 1–3(–4) mm. At present NO same-species local photo clearly isolates the TRUE INNER free membrane; do not use other Digitaria species' collar photos as exact evidence. Future source image must identify exact D. ciliaris and include a physical 1-mm ruler.
field_id_short_tiles.status: HIGHEST PRIORITY — EXACT-SPECIES INNER LIGULE MACRO PHOTO MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 02 · COLLAR, SHEATH AND BLADE HAIRS
field_id_short_tiles.short: No auricles; check which hairs belong to sheath/collar, versus blade surfaces.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Aboveground differentiation: D. ciliaris generally has a much hairier sheath/collar than the relatively hairless or sparsely hairy blade (local variation exists), no auricles, a roll-leaf vernation, and narrow parallel-veined blade. The inner jagged membrane must be distinguished from hairs at the OUTER leaf-sheath border and scattered papillose-based blade basal hairs. No existing species gallery panel proves those fine hairs at close range. Reference-only (not copied): USGS Plants of Louisiana exact-labelled exterior blade/sheath photos and UF IFAS Fig.8 true collar photo. Do not assert fine bristle angles without verifying licensed photographic pixels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: HIGH PRIORITY — VERIFIED OUTER COLLAR/SHEATH PHOTO WITH REUSE RIGHTS PENDING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 03 · FLOWERING HEAD — FINGERLIKE ONE-SIDED RACEMES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Typically 3–7 near-fingerlike, one-sided branches densely carrying spikelets.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Existing local species panels 2–3 (indices 1–2) visibly demonstrate several clustered one-sided racemes. Distinguish the WHOLE raceme (flowering branch) from its individual overlapping SPIKELETS; existing macros panel 5 (index 4) confirm attached one-sided spikelets. Unlike diffuse fall witchgrass, all flowering branches here look like fingers bearing tight aligned grains. These gross panels are already adequate; don't waste this pass adding more duplicate distant heads.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COVERED — REAL ATTACHED RACEMES, PANICLE AND SPIKELETS

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 04 · HIDDEN SIDE OF SPIKELET — UPPER GLUME
field_id_short_tiles.short: Examine the reverse face: upper glume proportion helps separate southern from large crabgrass.
field_id_short_tiles.details: Start with actual detached spikelet and scale background at panel 4 (index 3), plus attached branch at panel 5 (index 4). The upper glume occupies roughly 2/3–4/5 of a D. ciliaris spikelet in standard treatments and is usually over half its length; D. sanguinalis commonly has a shorter upper glume (often under half), though maturity/taxonomic variation matters. Existing photos do not positively show the reverse/hidden face: expose and photograph one verified mature spikelet from each taxon with a 1-mm scale and separate lower glume, upper glume, lower sterile lemma, and hard fertile lemma. Do not point exterior stripe arrows at an unsupported organ.
field_id_short_tiles.status: NEXT ANATOMY TARGET — TRUE HIDDEN UPPER GLUME AND DISSECTION STILL MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 05 · SHEATH/LIGULE COMPARISONS WITH CLOSE LOOK-ALIKES
field_id_short_tiles.short: Southern vs large vs smooth crabgrass; fall witchgrass has completely different flowering architecture.
field_id_short_tiles.details: D. sanguinalis is a VERY close look-alike and needs same-scale comparison of the inner ligule, broader blade hairs, and mature spikelet HIDDEN upper glume. D. ischaemum is often less hairy overall and has a less jagged membrane. Existing panels 6–8 (indices 5–7) instead show clearly labelled D. cognata, a different Digitaria with an open airy branching panicle. These contrast only flowering architectures; do NOT claim photographed D. sanguinalis glume comparison exists. Correct photo reference research: iNaturalist botanist Harry Rose article 'Separating Digitaria sanguinalis and Digitaria ciliaris', with named upper-glume and collar examples; independently verify each photo's source taxon and individual license BEFORE transferring pixels.
field_id_short_tiles.status: COGNATA COMPARISON COVERED — SANGUINALIS/ISCHAEMUM COLLAR PAIRS MISSING

field_id_short_tiles.heading: 06 · FINISH GATE — ABOVEGROUND FIRST; ROOTS LATER
field_id_short_tiles.short: Resolve true inner ligule, separate sheath hairs, then hidden glumes and lemma comparisons before root-node detail.
field_id_short_tiles.details: 5 actual exact-species locally archived JPEGs, 3 exact-labelled other-species comparison panels and 22 total existing broad arrows (14 own-species and 8 different-species). Existing head/spikelet architecture is useful. CURRENT PRIORITY: (1) exact source-confirmed true inner 1–3mm jagged membrane, (2) separate collar/sheath/base of blade hairs at millimeter macro, (3) both sides of a mature spikelet plus glumes and fertile/sterile lemmas, (4) same-scale D. sanguinalis/d. ischaemum reproductive comparison, (5) an authentic whole spreading plant with root-bearing lower node. No new photo is certified until photo-level CC/public rights and pixel review pass. Public Pages/mobile overlay verification is separate; no range/nativity inference from other states.
field_id_short_tiles.status: FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS — TRUE LIGULE AND MICRO-DIFFERENTIAL FIRST

grass_finalization.run_scope: Existing canonical Digitaria ciliaris only; practical Central Texas crew field ID, not new species or variety certification.
grass_finalization.LOOK_HERE_FIRST: Several clustered fingerlike one-sided racemes (often 3–7 in regional var. ciliaris treatment); inspect attached paired spikelets, then the true membranous ligule and mature glumes/lemmas. Do not determine from head shape alone.

measured_published_key.growth_form: Sprawling fibrous-rooted annual, sometimes rooting at decumbent lower nodes; this rooted connection is not proved by current gallery.
measured_published_key.racemes: Usually 3–7 fingerlike racemes, approximately 25–120 mm long in Williamson County var. ciliaris treatment.
measured_published_key.ligule: True membranous inner ligule about 1–3(–4) mm; no auricles; current gallery lacks calibrated opened-collar proof.
measured_published_key.spikelet_pairs: Two spikelets per rachis node, pedicels about 0.4–0.6 mm and 1.1–4.5 mm; current attached-branch photo does not measure both.
measured_published_key.lower_glume: About 0.3–0.4 mm, upper glume about 1.7–2 mm, generally 3-veined.
measured_published_key.sterile_lemma: Lower sterile lemma about 2.3–2.7 mm, usually (5–)7-veined; lateral nerve ornamentation matters against D. sanguinalis.
measured_published_key.fertile_lemma: Upper fertile lemma about 2.6–3.2 mm, palea around 2 mm; no long true lemma/glume awns.
measured_published_key.evidence_limit: Published regional var. ciliaris values, not measurements made from archived pixels; no variety determination or taxonomy/range change.

grass_finalization.lookalikes: D. cognata: airy panicle with widely spaced individually stalked spikelets (comparison panels 5–7). D. sanguinalis: similar fingerlike racemes, needs ripe sterile lower-lemma lateral-nerve ornamentation and hair examination. Eleusine indica: flattened fingers with multiflowered spikelets and often pale compressed base.
